tasks.user_prompt: A Client has an ordinary one-to-many Client.book relationship with Book, using Book.client_id as foreign key and no permanent relationship filter. Client 1 has Book 1 published on 2020-01-01 and Book 2 published on 2022-01-01. In one Session I first load Client 1 and its complete book collection. I then execute select(Client).outerjoin(Book, and_(Client.id == Book.client_id, Book.published < date(2021, 1, 1))).options(contains_eager(Client.book)).where(Client.id == 1), consuming session.scalars(stmt).unique().one(). Why can the returned collection still contain both books despite the filtered SQL? Explain and verify what changes when the same statement uses execution_options(populate_existing=True), and what happens after session.expire(client, ['book']) followed by access to client.book. State whether each query returns the same Client object. Assume pending changes are flushed; explain why that assumption matters. Trace identity-map lookup and the full-versus-partial population paths in this checkout, cite supporting source, and demonstrate all stages using an in-memory SQLite fixture.

claims.text: The filtered SQL yields only Book 1, but without populate_existing the already-loaded Client.book stays [1,2]; contains_eager routes explicit joined rows and does not automatically overwrite loaded attributes.
Rows resolve Client 1 through session_identity_map, so both filtered queries reuse the existing Client instance rather than allocating an independent client.
effective_populate_existing selects full population via _populate_full; otherwise an already present object uses the partial-population path and unloaded-state handling.
With populate_existing=True and flushed state, the filtered eager load overwrites the collection with only Book 1.
After expiring book, its normal unfiltered lazy load restores Books 1 and 2; the customized contains_eager contents are not permanent relationship configuration.
populate_existing can reset already-present state including pending changes, so data must be flushed first; ordinary Session autoflush is sufficient under its default behavior.

assertions.code:
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, '/workspace/lib')
import json
from datetime import date
import sqlalchemy
from sqlalchemy import create_engine, Integer, Date, ForeignKey, select, and_
from sqlalchemy.orm import DeclarativeBase, Mapped, mapped_column, relationship, Session, contains_eager
assert sqlalchemy.__file__.startswith('/workspace/')
class Base(DeclarativeBase):
    pass
class Client(Base):
    __tablename__ = 'client'
    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    book: Mapped[list['Book']] = relationship(order_by='Book.id')
class Book(Base):
    __tablename__ = 'book'
    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    client_id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(ForeignKey('client.id'))
    published: Mapped[date] = mapped_column(Date)
engine = create_engine('sqlite:///:memory:')
Base.metadata.create_all(engine)
with Session(engine) as seed:
    seed.add(Client(id=1, book=[Book(id=1, published=date(2020,1,1)), Book(id=2, published=date(2022,1,1))]))
    seed.commit()
with Session(engine) as session:
    client = session.get(Client, 1)
    before = [b.id for b in client.book]
    cutoff = date(2021,1,1)
    join_condition = and_(Client.id == Book.client_id, Book.published < cutoff)
    matching_sql_ids = list(session.scalars(select(Book.id).where(Book.client_id == 1, Book.published < cutoff)))
    stmt = select(Client).outerjoin(Book, join_condition).options(contains_eager(Client.book)).where(Client.id == 1).order_by(Book.id)
    first = session.scalars(stmt).unique().one()
    preserved = [b.id for b in first.book]
    session.flush()
    refreshed = session.scalars(stmt.execution_options(populate_existing=True)).unique().one()
    filtered = [b.id for b in refreshed.book]
    session.expire(client, ['book'])
    reloaded = [b.id for b in client.book]
    result = {'before':before, 'matching_sql_ids':matching_sql_ids, 'without_populate_existing':preserved, 'with_populate_existing':filtered, 'after_expire':reloaded, 'same_identity':first is client and refreshed is client}
print(json.dumps(result, sort_keys=True))
